description.narrative: Liberia Decentralization Support Program II (LDSP II), implemented by UNDP as the agreement partner for Sida, builds on previous support towards Liberia's decentralization process (LDSP I, 2016-2020). LDSP II has been running since 2020 and Sweden will enter as a donor during the period 2022-2024. Overall, the programme aims to reach the following outcomes: Outcome 1: LGA reforms implemented through enhanced participation of stakeholders (male, female, PWDs) in decision-making and service delivery, Outcome 2: Local government institutions and services are fully devolved at the assigned levels of government, Outcome 3: County Service Centers empowered and capacitated for improved service delivery at the sub-national level. Outcome 4: Legal and Regulatory Reforms developed and implemented to sustain decentralization. Outcome 5: Programme management support, coordination, and monitoring strengthened. Swedish support primarily focuses on fiscal decentralization.

Liberia Decentralization Support Programme II (LDSP II), som genomförs av UNDP som avtalspart för Sida, bygger på ett tidigare stöd till Liberias decentraliseringsprocess (LDSP I, 2016-2020). LDSP II har pågått sedan 2020 och Sverige kommer in som givare under perioden 2022-2024. Övergripande väntas insatsen bidra till följande resultat: 1. Reformer inom lagen för lokalförvaltning (Local Government Act) implementeras med ett ökat deltagande av rättighetsbärare (kvinnor, män och personer med funktionsvariationer) i beslutsfattande och i tillhandahållandet av tjänster 2. Lokala, statliga institutioner och tjänster är fullt ut delegerade till tilldelade myndighetsnivåer 3. Lokala servicekontor (County Service Centers) stärks och ges ökad kapacitet för förbättrad leverans av tjänster på lokal nivå 4. Rättsliga och regulatoriska reformer utvecklas och implementeras för att upprätthålla decentralisering 5. Stärkt programledningsstöd, samordning och uppföljning. Sveriges stöd till insatsen fokuserar främst på finansiell decentralisering.

description.narrative:
While the contribution from the Swedish embassy is primarily focusing on the fiscal decentralisation, Sweden is part of the basket fund and hence results from all areas of the program are included below.
Example of results during 2023:
- County Councils with a broad representation were established in all 15 Counties in line with Chapter 2 of the Local Government Act (LGA). This became possible because of sustained cooperation and engagements between the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Governance Commission, with support from the LDSP. The setup of the County Council completes one of the primary objectives of the LGA which creates a check and balance as it relates to accounting for development funds and local taxes raised. This was followed by County Council Orientation Workshops where members of the county councils together with Superintendents got to learn about their functions and responsibilities as well as clarified all misunderstandings around each stakeholders role at the subnational level.
- The Ministry of Internal Affairs with support from LDSP organized an Inter-Ministerial Committee on Decentralization meeting. The meeting brought together 29 participants including heads of decentralization Ministries, Agencies and Commissions (MACs), technicians, and development partners to critically look at all the issues facing the decentralization process and forge a way forward. This was an important milestone for strengthened commitments and improved coordination.
- Through the Letter of Agreement (LoA) between LRA and UNDP, the rollout and implementation of the Real Estate Tax collection could continue in Grand Bassa, district 3. After 90 tax agents were recruited, trained and deployed, they captured more than 2,650 properties.
- The solar power system has contributed to improved delivery of services, generation and consolidation of CSC reports, data collection and collation of reports, prevented theft at CSCs, improved CSCs staff attendance at work, and has improved the overall administrative operations of the county by providing power to the office of the superintendent.
- To strengthen the technical capacity of County Service Center staff to maintain Solar Power Systems, 25 technicians from 13 County Service Centers were trained. Apart from theoretical learning, the training also included practical assimilation exercises.
- Thanks to cooperation with civil society organisations, more than 3,500 people were directly educated (through town hall meetings, radio talk shows, debates and copies of distributed material) about the importance of the LGA and the decentralization reform progress thus far. This included development superintendents, city mayors, district commissioners, paramount chiefs, town chiefs, county council members, gender focal persons, as well as youth, women, and people with disabilities (PWDs)
- As a result of awareness raising about Citizen Feedback Mechanism (CFM) (through town hall meetings, communication material, jingles implemented by CSOs and CBOs) there was an increase in feedback coming in to the system. During the year more than 4,180 feedback entries were submitted to the system.
- Various types of trainings and workshops were organized to strengthen capacities within areas such as Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting (GRPB), Revenue Sharing Law and its benefits and obligations, Financial Management, and Monitoring and Evaluation.
- The Ministry of Transport window at the Margibi County Service Center was renovated, equipped, and services launched. Over the period, 543 vehicles were registered and generated LD $ 164,235.39 and USD 30,954.01. Similarly, 307 drivers license were registered and generated LRD 449,322.75 and USD 9,975.00 as revenue over the period. This shows the large demand for this service and an opportunity for revenue generation at local level once the Revenue Sharing Law is fully implemented.
